rewritten_query:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_month_seq = (
        SELECT d_month_seq
        FROM date_dim
        WHERE d_date = DATE '1999-02-11'
    )
),
ss_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           c.c_birth_year AS birth_year,
           SUM(ss.ss_ext_sales_price) AS ss_item_rev
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN params p ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = p.d_date_sk
    JOIN item i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN customer c ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 269 AND 298
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 57
      AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1938 AND 1944
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id, c.c_birth_year
),
cs_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           c.c_birth_year AS birth_year,
           SUM(cs.cs_ext_sales_price) AS cs_item_rev
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN params p ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = p.d_date_sk
    JOIN item i ON cs.cs_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN customer c ON cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    WHERE cs.cs_list_price BETWEEN 269 AND 298
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 57
      AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1938 AND 1944
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id, c.c_birth_year
),
ws_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           c.c_birth_year AS birth_year,
           SUM(ws.ws_ext_sales_price) AS ws_item_rev
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN params p ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = p.d_date_sk
    JOIN item i ON ws.ws_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN customer c ON ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    WHERE ws.ws_list_price BETWEEN 269 AND 298
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 57
      AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1938 AND 1944
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id, c.c_birth_year
),
combined AS (
    SELECT ss.item_id,
           ss.birth_year,
           ss.ss_item_rev,
           cs.cs_item_rev,
           ws.ws_item_rev,
           (ss.ss_item_rev + cs.cs_item_rev + ws.ws_item_rev) / 3.0 AS avg_rev
    FROM ss_items ss
    JOIN cs_items cs
      ON ss.item_id = cs.item_id
     AND ss.birth_year = cs.birth_year
    JOIN ws_items ws
      ON ss.item_id = ws.item_id
     AND ss.birth_year = ws.birth_year
    WHERE ss.ss_item_rev * 11 >= cs.cs_item_rev * 10
      AND ss.ss_item_rev * 10 <= cs.cs_item_rev * 11
      AND ss.ss_item_rev * 11 >= ws.ws_item_rev * 10
      AND ss.ss_item_rev * 10 <= ws.ws_item_rev * 11
      AND cs.cs_item_rev * 11 >= ws.ws_item_rev * 10
      AND cs.cs_item_rev * 10 <= ws.ws_item_rev * 11
)
SELECT item_id,
       birth_year,
       ss_item_rev,
       ss_item_rev / avg_rev * 100 AS ss_dev,
       cs_item_rev,
       cs_item_rev / avg_rev * 100 AS cs_dev,
       ws_item_rev,
       ws_item_rev / avg_rev * 100 AS ws_dev,
       avg_rev AS average
FROM combined
ORDER BY item_id, birth_year, ss_item_rev
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The date filter `d_date IN (SELECT d_date FROM date_dim WHERE d_month_seq = (SELECT ...))` was repeated in all three CTEs, causing repeated scans of date_dim and semi-joins. Replaced by a single `params` CTE computing the ~30 `d_date_sk` values for the target month once (materialized since referenced three times), joined directly on sales date SK. Score 9/10.

Converted old-style comma joins to explicit INNER JOIN ... ON syntax and replaced the redundant `date_dim` join per branch with a small hash join against `params` (~30 rows), leveraging the existing indexes on ss/cs/ws_sold_date_sk. Score 8/10.

The six symmetric BETWEEN ratio predicates (12 inequalities) were reduced to 6 exact inequalities. For a pair (A,B), `A BETWEEN 0.9B AND 1.1B AND B BETWEEN 0.9A AND 1.1A` is mathematically equivalent to `11*A >= 10*B AND 10*A <= 11*B` (i.e. A in [10/11·B, 11/10·B]). Applied to (ss,cs), (ss,ws), (cs,ws). Score 7/10.

The repeated expression `(ss_item_rev+cs_item_rev+ws_item_rev)/3` was computed once in a `combined` CTE as `avg_rev`, improving readability and avoiding repeated arithmetic; `combined` is referenced once so it is inlined with no materialization cost. Score 5/10.
Used the exact integer-multiplier form of the ratio bounds (×10/×11) instead of decimal constants, and explicit DATE literal, making bounds exact and evaluated once as constants. Score 4/10.
